{{Short description|Indian mathematician (1902–1988)}}
{{for|the educationist|Lala Hansraj Gupta}}
{{Use Indian English|date=April 2018}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2018}}
'''Hansraj Gupta''' (9 October 1902 &ndash; 23 November 1988) was an Indian [[mathematician]] specialising in [[number theory]], in particular the study of the [[partition (number theory)|partition function]].

==Biography==
Gupta was born 9 October 1902 in [[Rawalpindi]], then part of [[British India]]. His father was Gulraj Gupta, an executive engineer with the [[Bombay, Baroda and Central India Railway]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Reed|first1=Stanley|authorlink1=Stanley Reed (British politician)|title=The Indian And Pakistan Year Book And Who's Who 1950|date=1950|publisher=[[The Times Group|Bennett Coleman and Co. Ltd.]]|page=[https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.15206/page/n716 682]|url=https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.15206|accessdate=22 February 2018}}</ref> He studied at the [[Panjab University]] in [[Lahore]], where he graduated with a [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] in 1925. In 1928 he became a [[lecturer]] at the Government College in [[Hoshiarpur]]. He received his [[Ph.D.]] from the Panjab University in 1936. By then he had already published several papers on [[partition (number theory)|partitions]].{{citation needed|date=April 2018}}

Gupta was elected a [[fellow]] of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] (INSA) in 1950. He became head of the Panjab University's new department of [[mathematics]] in 1954. He served as president of the [[Indian Mathematical Society]] (IMS) for the term 1963&ndash;64.<ref>{{cite web | title = List of Office-Bearers | url = http://www.geocities.com/indianmathsociety/officebearers.htm | publisher = Indian Mathematical Society | accessdate = 2008-01-24 |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20091026042534/http://www.geocities.com/indianmathsociety/officebearers.htm| url-status = dead |archivedate=2009-10-26}}</ref> He retired as director of the Centre of Advanced Study in Mathematics in 1966, by which time he was already travelling [[North America]] as a [[visiting professor]]: at the [[University of Colorado at Boulder]] (1962), the [[University of Arizona]] (1966), and the [[University of Alberta]] (1969). He represented the INSA at the 1974 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Vancouver]]. He continued actively researching and publishing mathematics for many years after retirement.{{citation needed|date=April 2018}}

Gupta died 23 November 1988. Since 1990 the annual IMS conference has included a lecture in his honour, the Hansraj Gupta Memorial Award Lecture.<ref>{{cite web | title = IMS Memorial Award Lectures | url = http://www.geocities.com/indianmathsociety/memorialawardlectures.htm | publisher = Indian Mathematical Society | accessdate = 2008-01-24 |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20091026042528/http://www.geocities.com/indianmathsociety/memorialawardlectures.htm| url-status = dead |archivedate=2009-10-26}}</ref>
